a computerized training program, in combination with a fading protocol, improves the automaticity of postural control, as indicated by the reaction time in the dual task paradigm.
a postural training program with a fading protocol improves the ability to maintain posture while performing a concurrent task, but not the postural stability itself, as measured by sway.
a computerized postural training program, with a feedback fading procedure, improves automaticity of postural control and decreases attentional demands in the dual task.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an efficient training program to improve postural control in the elderly, which may lead to a decrease in the risk of falls.
a training program which is easy to implement and which can be used by a large population of the elderly.
the development and evaluation of a computerized feedback training program that is based on the principles of the motor learning process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the computerized feedback posturography training protocol is a useful tool to improve the automatic control of postural control.
the computerized training program used in this experiment is an efficient method to decrease the attentional demands required to perform postural tasks.
the computerized feedback posturography training with a feedback fading program can be used as a fall prevention strategy in older adults.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the training program was successful in improving balance and reaction time in the experimental group.

a computerized postural training program with a fading protocol can be used to improve posture in older adults and that the dual-task paradigm is a better measure of attentional demands during postural tasks than postural sway.
a computerized training protocol can improve the automaticity (efficiency) of posture and reduce the attentional demands of postural control in the elderly.

the dual-task paradigm may be more useful for evaluating the efficiency of fall prevention strategies.
the use of computerized feedback training with a fading protocol is a promising tool for improving the efficiency of posture and reducing attentional demands.
